hints: Read the wording very carefully. It does NOT ask how much total DNA is in prophase compared to G1, it asks how much of the original G1 DNA is still present later in the same cell.
Remember what happens in S phase (semi-conservative replication keeps both original strands) and remember that in telophase of mitosis cytokinesis has not yet split the cell in two.
walkthrough:
**Start with G1 and track the original DNA**

Think of G1 DNA as your starting set. Call it 100%.

The question is asking: of that starting set, how much is still inside that same cell later on? It is not asking for the total DNA content.

**From G1 to prophase: S phase doubles but keeps the original**

In S phase, each DNA molecule is replicated semi-conservatively. The two original strands stay and new strands are added alongside them.

So in prophase the cell has twice the total DNA, but 100% of the original G1 DNA is still there, now as part of the two-chromatid chromosomes.

**From prophase to telophase: still the same cell**

In anaphase the sister chromatids separate, and in telophase two nuclei reform. Crucially, cytokinesis has not yet divided the cytoplasm.

Both sets of chromosomes are still inside the one original parent cell, so 100% of the original G1 DNA is still present in that same cell. That gives 100% in prophase and 100% in telophase, option D.

options.A: Incorrect. This confuses halving at cell division with what is inside the single parent cell before cytokinesis is complete.
options.B: Incorrect. DNA is not lost going from G1 to prophase, the original strands are all conserved during S phase replication.
options.C: Incorrect. Telophase still has both daughter nuclei in the same cell, so no original DNA has left the cell yet, it is not 50%.
options.D: Correct. All the original G1 DNA is conserved through S phase into prophase, and both sets remain in the same cell through telophase before cytokinesis.
